# dott

CLI tool to check domain name availability. Direct WHOIS/RDAP lookups — no middlemen, no logging.

## commands

Check a name across all TLDs:
$ dott myname --plain

Check specific TLDs:
$ dott myname --tlds com,io,dev --plain

Check one full domain:
$ dott example.com --plain

Check several full domains through stdin:
$ printf '%s\n' example.com example.org | dott --plain

Suggest names from keywords:
$ dott --suggest keyword --plain

## output format

One domain per line: `<domain> <status>`

Status values: available, taken, protected, unknown

Example:
myname.com taken
myname.io available
myname.dev available
myname.co available

## notes

- Always use --plain for machine-readable output
- Plain output contains availability only; it does not fetch or include prices
- Use --tlds to narrow results and reduce output size
- Use --suggest when the user wants name ideas from a keyword
- A supplied full domain checks exactly that domain; --tlds applies only to bare names
- Invalid names and unsupported TLDs return a nonzero exit status and stderr diagnostics
- protected = registry indicates the name is blocked or reserved
- unknown = could not determine (treat as inconclusive)
- available = no registration found, not a guarantee of registrar sale or pricing
- Never treat unknown or protected as available
- Do not run --update or watchlist commands as part of a domain lookup
